mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan-source document path (exclusive and non-Hague): notarization by a Taiwan notary public; certification by the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF); verification by the designated notary society in mainland China under the Cross-Strait Notarization Agreement; certified Chinese translation. Hague Apostille and PRC Consular Legalization are inapplicable to Taiwan-source documents and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan-source document path (exclusive): Taiwan notarization; SEF certification; mainland PRC notary association verification; certified Chinese translation. No Apostille and no Consular Legalization path for Taiwan-source documents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE legal representative and incorporation signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan parent company, notarized before a Taiwan notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan-source document path (exclusive): Taiwan notarization; SEF certification; mainland PRC notary association verification; certified Chinese translation. If the resolution is executed by a parent in a Hague Apostille Convention member state: notarization plus Apostille issued by that state's competent authority, then certified Chinese translation. For a non-Hague and non-Taiwan state: notarization; Foreign Ministry legalization; PRC Embassy or Consulate consular legalization; certified Chinese translation. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative pathways and must never be applied sequentially.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), as amended, particularly Articles 98, 99, 100, 101, 108, 202, 206, 208, and 387; Foreign Investors Investment in Taiwan Permission Law, Articles 4, 7, and 10; and Mainland Investors Investing in Taiwan Permission Law, Article 8, where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company Registration One-Stop Service (FITI) of Taiwan.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration under Article 387 of the Company Act, together with the certified Articles of Incorporation, foreign investment approval certificate, and paid-in capital proof.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: There is no statutory minimum paid-up capital under Taiwan law. The Company may set its authorized paid-in capital in the Articles of Incorporation; all issued shares must be fully paid before incorporation registration. A foreign investor shall remit the approved capital into a Taiwan bank account and obtain a Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Certificate. No governmental blocked or escrow account is required; the subscription funds remain at risk in the Company's ordinary bank account and cannot be withdrawn to the shareholders except by lawful capital reduction or dividend distribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, THAT the following resolutions are adopted and recorded as the first Board of Directors resolution of the Company after issuance of the Certificate of Company Registration:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT. The authorized and paid-in share capital of the Company shall be as stated in the Articles of Incorporation to be filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs of Taiwan. The shareholders and directors present, holding full voting power, hereby unanimously accept the subscription of the entire issued capital and direct that the subscription amount be paid into a bank account opened in the name of the Company in Taiwan. Payment shall be evidenced by the bank's deposit certificate and the Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the receiving bank. No share shall be deemed fully paid unless the equivalent cash consideration has been received in cleared funds.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Chairman, acting with the General Manager, is hereby authorized to open, operate, and close corporate bank accounts, including New Taiwan Dollar and foreign currency accounts, with one or more financial institutions in Taiwan. The bank mandate shall require that any two authorized signatories, one of whom shall be the Chairman, sign checks, transfer orders, foreign exchange declarations, and electronic banking instructions. The same officers are authorized to execute account agreements, facility agreements, safe-deposit box contracts, and related banking documents for the exclusive benefit of the Company.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office of the Company shall be located at the address specified in the Articles of Incorporation and registered with the Ministry of Economic Affairs. The Chairman and General Manager are authorized to execute in the Company's name an office lease, utility agreements, building-use permits, and any municipal fire-safety inspection documents required for lawful office occupancy. The registered office shall be the principal place for service of process, maintenance of corporate books, and conduct of board meetings.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The following persons are appointed as the first statutory officers of the Company, to hold office until the next annual shareholders meeting: [Name] as Director and Chairman, [Name] as General Manager, and [Name] as Company Secretary and Chief Financial Compliance Officer. Each officer is vested with full authority to execute incorporation registrations, file tax and labor declarations, approve bank signatories, and represent the Company before administrative and judicial authorities. The General Manager may delegate day-to-day operational duties to employees in accordance with applicable labor law.

5. CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AUTHORITY. The Chairman shall maintain the registered office, minutes book, share register, corporate seal, and statutory record books. The Company seal shall be held under dual custody and may be affixed only with the prior written approval of the Chairman or General Manager. All statutory filings, tax forms, labor registrations, and licensing declarations executed following incorporation are hereby ratified in advance. This resolution is effective immediately upon the issuance of the Certificate of Company Registration and shall remain in full force until amended by a later board resolution or shareholder resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company and Business Registration One-Stop Service online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the official MOEA one-stop portal and apply for reservation of the proposed statutory company name and English trade name. Select the limited liability company form and declare the business scope aligned with ISIC 6201, namely software development, on-line language education, automated tutoring systems, and subscription-based EdTech services. Submit the foreign shareholder identity particulars and the intended registered office address. The system performs an automatic conflict check against the national company-name and trade-name database. Upon favorable review, the applicant obtains a name-reservation certificate valid for six months. This stage does not authorize business operations; the certificate must be attached to the subsequent incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Completed online name-reservation application
Passport or government-issued identification of the foreign investor representative
Power of attorney signed by the foreign parent company
Proposed statutory company name and romanized trade name
Intended business scope description referencing ISIC 6201
Preliminary registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to prior identical or confusingly similar registration, file a new alternative name through the same portal without delay. In exceptional cases, a formal appeal may be lodged with the MOEA Department of Commerce within thirty days of the adverse notice, but substitution of the name is the faster remedial course.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Commission Approval and Capital Remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Investment Review and Licensing Section, Taiwan.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal foreign investment application to the Investment Commission for a foreign or Mainland China parent entity. The Commission reviews the shareholder's legal existence, source of funds, intended business scope, national security implications, and economic contribution. After approval, the investor is issued an investment approval letter specifying the permitted amount and remittance period. The investor then remits the approved foreign currency from outside Taiwan through a designated bank, which issues a Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Certificate. This certificate is indispensable for the company registration submission and must be preserved in the original. For Mainland China investors, a stricter public-interest and security review is applied under the dedicated cross-strait investment regulations, and the Commission may impose additional conditions or prohibitions on sensitive sectors.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment application form signed by the investor
Certificate of incorporation and board resolution of the foreign parent company
Audited financial statements of the investor for the most recent fiscal year
Bank reference or proof of source of funds
Detailed investment plan and projected EdTech revenue model
Power of attorney appointing a Taiwan agent or attorney
Company name reservation certificate from step one
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a deficiency notice, the applicant must supply the requested supplementary information within the stated period, usually fourteen to thirty days, with a possible extension. If the application is ultimately refused, an administrative appeal to the Executive Yuan must be filed within thirty days, and the company formation process is suspended until final determination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan-licensed attorney or certified public accountant, with authentication by a Taiwan notary public where required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the statutory form for a limited company under the Taiwan Company Act. The Articles must state the company name, registered office address, business scope, total authorized capital, paid-up capital, classes of shares if any, number of directors, appointment of officers, duration, and procedural rules for amendment. Every shareholder must sign all pages of the document; a foreign corporate shareholder must provide notarized and apostilled corporate resolutions and identification, together with a local translation where required. The responsible attorney or accountant must verify that the Articles do not conflict with mandatory provisions of Taiwanese law, particularly rules on capital payment, directors' duties, and foreign ownership. Once fully executed, the Articles become the binding constitutional document of the Company and are submitted with the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in the statutory language
Shareholder subscription and consent statement
Certified and apostilled board resolution of the foreign parent
Passport copies and corporate identification of subscribing shareholder
Statement of consent to act signed by each director and manager
Power of attorney authorizing the Taiwan legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or accountant identifies a defect in the execution or authentication, the document must be re-executed or re-authenticated before filing. Where the Articles contain a provision contrary to mandatory law, the Board must amend the Articles and obtain fresh shareholder signatures before any registration step proceeds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration at the MOEA One-Stop Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company Registration One-Stop Service (FITI).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the foreign investment approval has been issued and capital remitted, submit the complete incorporation file to the MOEA through the online one-stop portal or in person at the designated service window. The submission must include the application for company registration, the executed Articles of Incorporation, the name-reservation certificate, the paid-in capital proof in the form of a bank deposit certificate or foreign exchange inward remittance certificate, the lease agreement or building owner consent for the registered office, and identification documents for all directors and officers. The MOEA reviews the file for legal compliance, consistency between the Articles and the filed business scope, lawful capital contribution, and proper authorization of the foreign investor. Upon favorable review, the MOEA issues the Certificate of Company Registration and assigns the statutory company identification number. The Company becomes a juridical person on the date of the certificate.
required_dossiers: Application for company registration
Foreign investment approval certificate from the Investment Commission
Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Certificate or paid-in capital proof
Executed Articles of Incorporation
Company name reservation certificate
Registered office lease or owner's consent and proof of lawful use
Director and officer identification documents
Power of attorney for the Taiwan filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA issues a correction notice, the applicant must cure all deficiencies within the response window and resubmit the revised documents through the online system. If the application is refused, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the MOEA within thirty days or refile an entirely corrected application; a new filing fee may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Tax, Labor, and Banking Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (jurisdiction office) under the Ministry of Finance, municipal labor and building authorities, and the selected commercial bank in Taiwan.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Certificate of Company Registration, complete the mandatory post-incorporation filings. Register the Company for enterprise taxation with the National Taxation Bureau in the district of the registered office to obtain a Uniform Invoice Number and corporate tax filing status. Open the primary New Taiwan Dollar operating bank account and any foreign currency account required by the business plan by presenting the certificate of incorporation, Articles, board resolution, signatory identification, and banking reference. Register employees for labor insurance and file the new-employee list with the municipal labor inspection office. Since the business is a digital EdTech and software development company, no factory, warehouse, chemical, or manufacturing registration is applicable. The office must still satisfy fire-safety and building-use requirements under local municipal codes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Company Registration
Certified Articles of Incorporation
Director and manager identification documents
Board resolution appointing bank signatories
Uniform Invoice Number tax registration form
Office lease contract and building-use permit
Labor insurance registration forms for expected employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration office queries the address or representative, provide the updated lease, power of attorney, and board resolution. If a bank refuses account opening due to incomplete beneficial ownership information, correct the shareholder ownership chart and resubmit the same registration certificate; if labor registration is suspended, cure the employee identity and contract documentation and request re-submission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 6201 software development, on-line language education, and automated tutoring do not trigger the Factory Management Act registration regime or any industrial development authority permit for manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating license is required for a digital EdTech company. The Company must nevertheless hold company registration and tax registration with a Uniform Invoice Number to lawfully provide software subscription services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - if a physical development were proposed, the responsible agency would be the Environmental Protection Administration of the Executive Yuan, Taiwan, but no such development is proposed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the EdTech software business does not fall under any Article 4 or Article 5 development category of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, and no EIA screening, registration, or full EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no process wastewater, volatile organic compound releases, or hazardous waste generation will occur. The office premises must comply with ordinary municipal sanitary sewer standards for domestic wastewater, if any, and standard solid waste collection laws applicable to office occupancies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as an industrial civil-defense license. The registered office must, however, comply with the Taipei City Fire Prevention Act inspection requirements, maintain fire extinguishers and evacuation signage, and satisfy the general workplace safety duties of the Occupational Safety and Health Act for computer-based, low-risk office employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (Taiwan), represented by the National Taxation Bureau regional system and the Customs Administration; principal online tax portals: Ministry of Finance Tax Portal (tax.nat.gov.tw) and the e-Invoice Integration Service Platform (einvoice.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: A foreign non-resident entity must appoint a Taiwan-resident responsible person or branch manager and secure a physical Taiwan business address. Step 2: If the entity creates a branch or place of business in Taiwan, complete branch registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs; the MOEA approval is a precondition for tax registration. Step 3: File profit-seeking enterprise tax registration with the local National Taxation Bureau under Article 28 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act within the statutory period after commencement, submitting the MOEA registration certificate, duly authenticated foreign incorporation documents, local address proof, representative appointment, and bank account details. Step 4: The National Taxation Bureau issues the Business Tax Registration Certificate and assigns the Unified Business Number (UBI), which is the statutory TIN used for income tax, business tax, customs, and e-Invoice filings. Step 5: For a foreign electronic services provider without a fixed Taiwan place of business that sells B2C e-services such as app-store-distributed language-learning subscriptions to Taiwan consumers, file simplified business tax registration with the Ministry of Finance under Article 28-1 of the Business Tax Act; the MOF assigns a TW-prefixed Business Tax Registration Number and requires quarterly returns and payment through the MOF online system. Step 6: Register as an e-Invoice filer on the MOF e-Invoice Platform, establish API or Turnkey transmission credentials, and appoint a tax agent where required for ongoing compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not have a check-the-box pass-through election, consolidated income tax filing, or statutory hybrid-mismatch election; a profit-seeking enterprise or branch is taxed at the entity level on Taiwan-source income. The only electively relevant VAT mechanism is the simplified registration/quarterly filing regime available to foreign electronic services providers without a fixed Taiwan establishment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax, commonly referred to as Taiwan Business Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general monetary turnover threshold for Taiwanese domestic sellers or local branches; registration is mandatory before any taxable sale. For foreign electronic services providers without a fixed Taiwan place of business, simplified registration is mandatory when annual B2C e-service sales to Taiwan customers exceed TWD 480,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan requires VAT-registered businesses to issue Uniform Invoices for each taxable sale, and e-Invoice data must be transmitted to the MOF e-Invoice Integration Service Platform via API/Turnkey integration in MOF-specified formats. The platform assigns unique invoice numbers and random anti-fraud codes/QR codes and reconciles e-Invoice data with VAT returns and customs/export records. Taiwan does not use a physical fiscal-lock/stamping device, but accepted e-Invoice transmission constitutes the fiscal clearance event, with unreported or unmatched invoices generating automated audit flags.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, zero rating applies to goods physically exported from Taiwan, services directly connected with exports, and services supplied to a foreign person for use entirely outside Taiwan. A VAT-registered EdTech subscription business claiming 0% must issue a zero-rated Uniform Invoice and substantiate that the language-learning service is delivered to and consumed by a non-Taiwan final user. For app-store distribution, the platform settlement reports, billing-country data, geolocation/IP evidence, and foreign-currency remittance are required to prove foreign consumption; absent such evidence, Taiwan VAT at 5% is assessed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export bill of entry) accepted by the Customs Administration for physical goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing export from Taiwan to the foreign destination
Zero-rated Uniform Invoice issued to the overseas buyer
Commercial invoice and signed service contract identifying the foreign purchaser and place of use/consumption
Bank foreign-currency receipt or settlement certificate, or foreign remittance payment advice, evidencing collection from the foreign buyer
App-store or platform sales report with user billing-country, geolocation, and transaction timestamps for digital EdTech services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau and the Customs Administration cross-check export declarations, e-Invoice records, app-store merchant reports, and bank foreign-exchange receipts. Zero-rating is reversed if the goods are not supported by a valid export declaration or the foreign-currency proceeds are not received within the statutory 180-day repatriation period, or if digital-service evidence does not demonstrate consumption outside Taiwan; reassessed VAT at 5%, late interest, and penalties will be charged. Under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, false, fraudulent, or unsubstantiated zero-rating/refund claims attract a penalty of not less than five and not more than fifteen times the evaded tax, and fraudulent conduct is additionally subject to criminal liability and retrospective clawback audit recovery for seven years under the Tax Collection Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) acting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China maintains a managed floating exchange-rate regime under which the RMB is convertible only for current-account transactions, while capital-account transactions remain subject to restrictive licensing, registration, and authenticity checks. Inbound direct investment from a Taiwan shareholder into the CN_WFOE_LTD is classified as a capital-account receipt and therefore requires full FDI foreign-exchange registration under SAFE rules, the opening of a designated foreign-exchange capital account at a SAFE-authorized domestic bank, and the subsequent conversion of the registered capital into RMB only for genuine underlying obligations that are within the permitted negative-list scope. Current-account items, such as EdTech subscription revenues, software licensing fees, and operating expenses, are generally convertible, but the domestic bank must validate each payment using contracts, commercial invoices, tax documentation, and available customs or digital records. Dividend and profit repatriation to the Taiwanese parent is permissible after the annual statutory audit, but requires audited financial statements, corporate income-tax payment proof, a formal shareholder dividend resolution, and the use of SAFE-approved payment rails. Borrowing from offshore related parties triggers the PBOC macro-prudential full-cycle constraint, and any external guarantee, cross-border financing, or capital injection must be tracked by the bank and SAFE. The practical result is stringent, multi-layered regulatory surveillance of every cross-border remittance, with no silent free movement of RMB outside the permitted current-account and registered capital channels.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current PRC regulations, there is no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; enterprises may retain export receipts in a foreign-currency current-account balance or sell them for RMB at a designated bank. However, exporters are required to repatriate export proceeds to the PRC within the statutory verification period, generally 180 days from the date of customs export declaration unless an extension has been approved by SAFE. The receiving bank must perform electronic matching against the customs declaration through the International Trade Single Window, and any unexplained non-payment or late recovery must be justified with a qualified bank statement and underlying contract before the export verification is closed.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs, including Wise, Airwallex, and Payoneer, are not legally viable as a primary treasury or account-raising channel for a China-incorporated WFOE. These entities do not hold PBOC or SAFE licences to open RMB settlement accounts, receive export proceeds, or perform China foreign-exchange declaration and tax reconciliation for a PRC legal person. They can only operate as ancillary ancillary payment intermediaries for certain outbound low-value supplier payments when a licensed domestic bank remains the master account provider. All inbound capital injections and export proceeds for the WFOE must ultimately settle into a bank licensed under PBOC/SAMR rules; therefore, fintech EMI-only onboarding is structurally barred and must be avoided.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical branch presence is effectively mandatory for opening an FDI capital account and an RMB basic deposit account. The legal representative or a duly authorised finance officer must appear in person at the bank, present original identity documents, provide the company seal and legal representative seal, and complete the initial KYC interview. For a Taiwan-incorporated shareholder or legal representative who cannot travel, a notarized power of attorney may be accepted only after cross-strait SEF/ARATS or consular legalization, and the bank will ordinarily still require a live video verification call with the legal representative. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted under PBOC account-opening rules; in practice, Tier-1 banks require at least one in-person signing for the corporate account mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity due to the Taiwan-based holding structure and potential nominee-shareholder arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and SEF/ARATS-authenticated Taiwan company registration and articles of incorporation; complete ultimate beneficial ownership identification through shareholder registers; audited financial statements of the Taiwanese parent for the last two years; source-of-wealth proof for the capital contribution such as tax returns, dividend certificates, capital gains statements, or banking evidence; a board resolution approving the WFOE investment; and certified copies of the ultimate shareholders passports or Taiwan identity certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital-only EdTech entity with minimal physical substance, creating shell-company or transaction-laundering concern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RMB registered-office lease or property ownership certificate; payroll and Chinese social insurance contribution records for operating staff; periodic VAT and corporate income tax returns; original commercial invoices and tax fapiao issued to Apple/Google for platform distributions; software developer registration and app-store listings; monthly subscription user and revenue dashboards; server hosting agreements; and an internal memorandum documenting the WFOE's operating substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear settlement trail from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing through third-party payment aggregators and out-of-name collection accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed Apple Developer Program Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement signed by the WFOE; monthly payout statements and aggregate settlement reports from both platforms; a payment-flow diagram showing app-store collection, payment gateway custody, and final settlement to the onshore bank account; invoices and revenue-recognition accounting entries; chargeback and refund history; and an auditor attestation confirming no third-party collection for unrelated entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Global app-store distribution to sanctioned or restricted jurisdictions and IP/export-control leakage risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written OFAC, EU, UN and PRC sanctions compliance policy; proof of geolocation and IP address blocking controls; no-restricted-party-attestation from management; export-control and encryption classification self-assessment; data-residency and privacy-compliance certifications; a customer approval matrix; and sanitized sanctions-screening logs covering app-store territories.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital from the Taiwanese shareholder must be wired via SWIFT MT103 to the CN_WFOE_LTD's SAFE-verified FDI foreign-exchange capital account at a designated Tier-1 bank. The remittance must reference the SAFE foreign-investment registration code and the receiving bank must classify it as inbound direct-investment capital injection using the applicable SAFE purpose code. The bank will perform negative-list screening, currency convertibility registration, and payment-amount verification against the approved registered capital. After receipt, a Chinese CPA must issue a capital-verification opinion; the proceeds are then converted into RMB in the capital settlement account and may be used only for genuine operating purposes such as payroll, rent, software procurement, cloud services, and platform distribution fees within the approved business scope.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound operational and trade disbursements, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers, covering EdTech platform fees, advertising, cloud infrastructure, software licences, and intercompany service fees. The bank will require the underlying contract, commercial invoice, tax withholding certificate, proof of service receipt, and an appropriate SAFE purpose declaration before release. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are permissible for physical goods import or export, but are not the normal rail for digital subscription services; when used, the bank must align the documentary presentation with the customs bills of lading and the SAFE cargo verification system. All outbound payments are submitted through the bank's electronic banking portal and monitored under the cross-border payment and tax reconciliation framework.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CNY/USD deliverable forward contracts with onshore designated banks, supported by documented current-account exposure or registered foreign-currency debt service obligations
CNY/USD FX swaps executed onshore for short-term liquidity and conversion-leakage management under SAFE-approved underlying transactions

Plain-vanilla CNY/USD currency options onshore, captured under a CFETS/ISDA master agreement and strictly hedging existing and documented trade or service exposures without speculative position limits

NDFs are not permissible for the onshore WFOE unless specifically approved with SAFE registration and an underlying offshore CNH asset or cross-currency exposure; TWD deliverable forwards may be considered with a Taiwanese counterparty bank only for genuine cross-strait trade/royalty flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking Enterprise Income Tax Final Return and Retained Earnings Surtax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance - National Taxation Bureau of Taiwan (district tax office at the WFOE's registered address)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due from 1 May through 31 May of the immediately following calendar year; for a fiscal year ending 31 December 202X, the final filing deadline is 31 May 202X+1. A valid extension can be applied for before 31 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after the 31 May statutory deadline triggers a late-filing surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax (minimum New Taiwan dollars 1,500, maximum New Taiwan dollars 30,000), daily interest at the Postal Savings Bank of Taiwan one-year fixed deposit rate, and, if the tax is understated intentionally, penalties up to the amount of underpaid tax plus imprisonment. A wholly dormant enterprise that fails to file for a full year may be reported by the tax authority to the Company Registration Office for administrative deregistration under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Tax (Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax) Periodic Returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance - National Taxation Bureau of Taiwan (district tax office for the principal place of business)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six bi-monthly filing periods: Jan-Feb due 15 Mar; Mar-Apr due 15 May; May-Jun due 15 Jul; Jul-Aug due 15 Sep; Sep-Oct due 15 Nov; Nov-Dec due 15 Jan of the next year. Each due date may be shifted to the next business day if it falls on a holiday.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a periodic business tax return by the 15th triggers a late-filing penalty of New Taiwan dollars 1,200, increased to New Taiwan dollars 3,000 for a second or later late filing in the same year, plus daily interest on the tax due. Understatement of output tax, excessive input tax credits, or false e-invoice records can produce penalties of up to five times the underpaid tax and suspension of the tax registration, leading ultimately to strike-off of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Shareholders Meeting: Approval of Business Report, Financial Statements, and Profit Distribution Proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing is required for a non-public WFOE; the signed minutes, attendance sheets, and all supporting financial statements must be maintained in the statutory Minute Book at the Taiwan head office and made available to the Company Registration Office, the National Taxation Bureau, and the Investment Commission on demand.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year WFOE the ordinary meeting must be convened no later than 30 June. If profit distribution is proposed, payment of dividends to the foreign parent typically follows the meeting and the remittance report is due within 10 days thereafter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure of the board of directors to convene the ordinary meeting within the six-month window exposes each responsible director to an administrative fine of New Taiwan dollars 10,000 to 100,000 under the Company Act enforcement regime. The Company Registration Office may order the meeting to be convened within a specified period; repeated non-convening, coupled with inactivity for more than six months, is a mandatory administrative dissolution trigger under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Filing of CPA-Audited Financial Statements and Updated Corporate/Registration Records with the Company Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs - Company Registration Office of Taiwan (central or regional service center)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the annual shareholders' ordinary meeting approves the financial statements; for a calendar-year WFOE holding the meeting on 30 June, the filing is due by 30 July. The same filing obligation applies upon any change of directors, shareholders, registered address, or capital, subject to a 15-day change-registration window under the Company Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the required audited financial statements or updated registration data triggers a rectification order and administrative penalties of New Taiwan dollars 10,000 to 500,000; continued non-compliance for more than six months can cause MOEA to strike the company off the commercial register, with consequent loss of legal personality and liquidation by operation of law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Implementation and Beneficial Ownership Information Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs - Investment Commission of Taiwan (foreign-invested WFOE supervision unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end, i.e. by 30 June for a calendar-year WFOE, unless a shorter anniversary window (such as the company incorporation date) is stated in the foreign investment approval letter. Changes in the foreign shareholding structure, ultimate owners, or approved investment amount must additionally be reported within 15 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Investment Commission may issue a warning or rectification order and impose fines under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals; where the foreign investor fails to execute the approved investment or ceases operations, the Commission may revoke the investment approval, and the Taiwan WFOE will be compelled to dispose of its assets or complete liquidation within the ordered period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Withholding Tax Return and Remittance Report on Dividends Distributed to the Foreign Corporate Parent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance - National Taxation Bureau of Taiwan (as the withholding agent's tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 10 days after the dividend payment is actually made or remitted to the foreign corporate shareholder; where the dividend is paid immediately after the ordinary shareholders' meeting, the practical due date is within the 10-day period following the payment date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to withhold the statutory withholding tax on dividends paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder exposes the WFOE to a penalty equal to the under-withheld amount plus daily interest; failure to file the withholding return itself is separately penalized with New Taiwan dollars 1,500 to 15,000, and intentional non-withholding may be prosecuted as tax evasion.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 20 of Taiwan's Company Act, a non-public Taiwan company, including a foreign-invested WFOE, must have its annual financial statements audited and certified by an independent licensed CPA when paid-in capital reaches New Taiwan dollars 30 million or more (approximately USD 950,000). A balance-sheet trigger also exists for designated supervised enterprises: banks, insurance companies, securities and futures firms, and companies whose registration or industry license requires FSC/MOEA oversight must be CPA-audited irrespective of size. No employee-headcount threshold is separately codified in the Company Act audit mandate; however, the tax and labor authorities may require audited statements from an enterprise with turnover over New Taiwan dollars 100 million (approximately USD 3.2 million) or more than 100 employees for financial-strength verification under the Income Tax Act and Business Entity Accounting Act. Public companies listed or traded on the Taiwan Stock Exchange or Taipei Exchange are always subject to IFRS and independent CPA audits under the Securities and Exchange Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For public companies, Taiwan-IFRS (the Financial Supervisory Commission's endorsed IFRS framework) is mandatory. For a non-public WFOE, the governing local GAAP framework is the Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (TFRS for SMEs) read together with the Business Entity Accounting Act and the Regulations Governing Business Accounting Handling; the company may voluntarily elect full Taiwan-IFRS. Statutory books and supporting vouchers must be maintained in Chinese-language records, and the financial statements must be expressed in New Taiwan Dollars, with English translation permitted for the PRC parent group if prepared as consolidated-packaging schedules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan's Company Act does not impose a separate filed annual beneficial ownership return form for a non-public WFOE. Instead, the Money Laundering Control Act requires the Taiwan WFOE to maintain a beneficial-ownership register at its head office and to notify the Company Registration Office of any change in ultimate beneficial ownership within 15 days. The corporate secretary must therefore run an annual UBO confirmation no later than 31 May, reconcile the internal shareholder register with the foreign parent's chain of ownership, and file any updated registers within the 15-day change window. Under Company Act Article 165, the board may close the register of members for up to 30 days before the ordinary shareholders' meeting; during that register-close period no share transfers are recorded and any transfers delivered after the record date are effective only for the following year, so all share-transfer documentation for a calendar-year WFOE should be processed and registered before the AGM by 30 June.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% of taxable net income for profit-seeking enterprises, plus a 5% undistributed-surplus surtax on retained earnings not distributed in the following year, producing an approximate effective cash corporate tax of 24% if the EdTech WFOE retains its profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No patent-box regime is available for language-learning software; ordinary subscription income is fully taxed. A Taiwan WFOE may claim a 10% to 15% investment tax credit on qualified research and development expenditures under Article 10 of the Statute for Industrial Innovation, capped at 30% of the profit-seeking enterprise tax liability; accelerated depreciation on software development and certain free-trade-zone incentives are available only after express approval, and the foreign parent in mainland China cannot obtain a Taiwan tax holiday for the WFOE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form 105) and Related Party Transactions Disclosure (Form 105Z), filed through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance electronic tax filing portal. The Taiwan-resident WFOE files Form 105; a non-resident parent with a Taiwan permanent establishment files the separate non-resident enterprise income tax return (Form 105-II) through an authorised tax agent, and the WFOE acts as withholding agent for non-resident dividends, interest, royalties and service fees through the electronic withholding tax system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement filing plus a provisional (tentative) tax payment on first-half-year taxable income due by September 30; quarterly CIT instalments are not prescribed, but VAT returns and monthly withholding remittances are separate compliance obligations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on December 31, the annual Form 105 return and final tax payment must be filed by May 31 of the following year; the provisional tax payment for the first half-year is due within two months after the close of that half-year period, i.e. by September 30.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross transaction revenue from sales and services, including gross subscription revenue from the EdTech language-learning app, digital content, licensing and customisation; Apple IAP and Google Play Billing commissions must not reduce gross turnover.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all Taiwan-source app subscription receipts. If a foreign parent sells directly to Taiwan consumers, the parent must have a Taiwan PE and file Form 105-II; otherwise the WFOE must report the Taiwan-source revenue for the foreign parent and comply with the applicable non-resident withholding rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold / cost of services sold, including platform commissions, content licensing acquisition costs, cloud hosting, engineering content costs and amortisation of capitalised software development.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany content and cloud-service costs are deductible only if supported by a transfer pricing report and actual economic benefit; an addback is required for excessive intra-group royalty payments under Income Tax Act Article 43-1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit (gross subscription revenue less Box 2 costs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A sustained gross margin significantly below the comparable EdTech interquartile range will trigger a transfer pricing audit, especially where the foreign parent owns IP and charges royalties to the WFOE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: personnel, marketing, administrative, R&D, trademark and royalty payments, headquarter service charges, depreciation and miscellaneous fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties and head office charges paid to the non-resident shareholder must be reported as deductible expenses but are subject to 20% withholding tax and must meet the arm's length standard; the parent's Tax Residency Certificate and Beneficial Ownership Declaration are required for any treaty rate reduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating revenue and expenses, such as interest income, interest expense, foreign exchange gains and losses, asset disposal gains and losses, and investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Passive interest paid to non-resident related lenders is subject to 20% withholding; excess interest on related-party debt exceeding the statutory debt-to-equity ratio of 3:1 is nondeductible under Article 43-2 and must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss carryforward: Box 3 margin reduced by Box 4 and Box 5.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing, thin-capitalisation and anti-abuse adjustments must be included; a non-resident parent cannot simply impose a guaranteed profit margin on the WFOE, and the WFOE must realise an arm's length operating profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year loss deduction from approved profit-seeking enterprise losses carried forward for ten years under Income Tax Act Article 39.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss must be evidenced by an approved tax return and the WFOE must have maintained proper accounting records; losses cannot be transferred from the foreign parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This amount is eligible for foreign tax credit only if the income is foreign-source to the Taiwan WFOE; the Chinese parent's foreign tax credit in its own jurisdiction is not reflected on Form 105.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Regular income tax at 20% plus the remaining undistributed-surplus tax of 5% where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE does not distribute its surplus, the 5% undistributed earnings surtax is imposed at the entity level; if it distributes to the non-resident parent, the WFOE must withhold 21% from the cash dividend and remit it to the National Taxation Bureau.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and prepayments: retained withholding tax, tentative tax payments, investment tax credits and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty-reduced rates are claimed through the domestic withholding tax return rather than Box 10, because the beneficiary is the non-resident shareholder; for Taiwan-Mainland China payments, no effective bilateral treaty rate is currently available, so the Chinese parent must rely on unilateral foreign tax credit in its home jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 105 triggers a surcharge under the Tax Collection Act, commonly calculated as 1% of the tax due for every two days of delinquency up to 15%, together with monthly late-filing surcharges under Income Tax Act Article 108; under Article 110, an underpayment caused by misstatement is penalised at twice the shortfall amount; fraudulent cross-border profit shifting and false transfer pricing documents become criminal under Tax Collection Act Article 41, carrying imprisonment, detention and fines; failure to file Form 105Z after notice may produce fines up to NT$300,000 and an evidentiary burden shift against the taxpayer.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on gross cash dividends and 21% on stock dividends valued at par or paid-in amount when distributed by the Taiwan WFOE to a foreign corporate shareholder not maintaining a Taiwan registered branch; this withholding is separate from the 20% CIT and the 5% undistributed-surplus surtax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: If an applicable bilateral tax treaty is in force, the receiving non-resident shareholder must, before the payment date, provide the WFOE and the National Taxation Bureau with: (i) a current-year Tax Residency Certificate issued by the shareholder's home tax
